p.t: In short
Build **five pages** on your store before you open any ad or shop account.
The five pages are: privacy policy, terms, contact page, shipping policy, and refund/return policy.

A missing page can get your Google account **suspended** (paused).
Read every generated text yourself before you publish it.
**Two working ways to contact you** must appear on your contact page and in the footer, and both must be real. Email plus phone is the safe choice.
**Remove every placeholder** (dummy text, square brackets, "555" phone numbers) before you publish any policy.
**Use the same policy text** on your site pages and in the checkout settings, and link every policy in the footer.

**Check each policy with AI, one page at a time.** Send the pasted text, not the live site. Have a lawyer check custom cases.
Put the **company name and email** on every legal page.

Show the **refund rules and shipping rules** in checkout before visitors arrive.
Link the policy pages in the **footer** before you run any ads.

In Germany, the **Impressum** must be complete before the store goes live.
Your **Terms of Service and Privacy Policy** must be live before launch.
Store policies and legal pages
Store policies and legal pages
The required set differs by source and by platform. Each source's list is kept below, so you can see what it asks for.
p.h: Which pages are required, by source

p.t: **Google Merchant Center approval (Google's account that lists your products for sale)**
Required set: **Four**: privacy policy (how customer data is used), terms of service (the rules for using the site and buying), shipping policy, refunds/returns/exchanges policy

Context: Approval requirement for ecommerce stores
**Five pages before opening accounts**
Required set: Privacy policy, terms and conditions, contact page, shipping policy, refund/return policy
Context: Before Google Merchant Center, Google Ads (Google's paid ads), Microsoft Advertising (Microsoft's paid ads), Facebook Ads (paid ads on Facebook and Instagram),

or the Facebook Shop channel (your shop on Facebook)
Ids: ,
**Footer list before traffic (visitors to your site)**
Required set: Privacy policy, terms and conditions, contact us, shipping policy, refunds and exchanges

Context: Create and link in the footer (the strip at the bottom of every page) before sending traffic
**Four footer-linked policies**

Required set: Return/refund policy, shipping policy, privacy policy, terms of service
Context: **All four** must exist and be linked in the footer
**Google Ads core pages**

Required set: Privacy policy, terms of service, returns and refunds
Context: Add before running paid traffic
**Supplier-ready store**
Required set: About Us, Contact Us, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service
Context: Before supplier outreach (contacting the companies that ship your products); privacy and terms are also required for a store that runs ads

**Launch gate**
Required set: Shipping policy, refund policy, privacy policy
Context: Missing any of these should **block the launch**

**Pre-launch**
Required set: Privacy policy, terms of service, contact information, refund or return policy

Context: The pages shoppers look for and that Shopify (the online store software) links at checkout (the payment step)
**Written policies**

Required set: Return and refund policy, privacy policy, terms of service, shipping policy, contact information
Context: Each shows "No policy set" until added
**Full legal section**
Which pages are required, by source (continued)
Required set: Terms and conditions, shipping and delivery, returns and exchanges, customer service and complaint handling, data privacy and security

Context: Every page must describe what the shop **really does**
**Cross-border store (you sell into other countries)**
Required set: Privacy, terms of service, returns and refunds, shipping, payment terms (the rules for paying), contact details

Context: Builds trust, shows compliance (following the rules), helps resolve disputes with customers and payment providers
**Checkout minimum**
Required set: Refund and shipping pages with company name and at least an email address; privacy and terms are secondary but good to have

Context: Pages shown in checkout
**Shopify list**

Required set: Return policy, privacy policy, terms of service, shipping policy, contact information
Context: Shown under Settings > Policies

**Build five pages**: privacy, terms, contact, shipping, refund/return. These cover every list above.
Add payment terms too. The cross-border list requires them.

Add About Us if you will approach suppliers.
Launch with **all required pages live**.
A missing privacy policy can get your Google Merchant Center account suspended. Repeated violations can lead to a ban (permanent closure).

Merchant Center flags your account by itself when pages are missing.
You must then **request a manual review** (a person checks it). This slows the process.
**Create the pages first**, before opening any ad or merchant account. This helps avoid suspensions and closures.
Google Merchant Center asks you to **confirm** that you read the policies. You also confirm that the account follows them.
**These pages do not make the store fully compliant** (following all the rules). Each platform handles other topics in its own setup.
You can refine policies **after** supplier deals are final. The launch goal is "supplier-ready" (working well enough for suppliers), not perfect.
Policies must be **published on the site**. They must match what you enter in Google Merchant Center.
Policies must be **easy to find**. Some ad platforms need easy access before they approve ads. Otherwise they may refuse to run them.
Privacy policy and terms of service must **match what Google Ads requires**.
Work order in Shopify: Compliance setup order (complete sequence)
**Generate** the privacy policy with Shopify's privacy policy generator (a free tool that writes the text for you). Answer the company questions. Then request the document by email.
2. **Add** the required extra privacy text to the generated policy, if it is missing.
A remarketing sentence (remarketing means showing ads again to past visitors) at the end of the introduction or closing.
A Google Analytics sentence (Google Analytics is Google's visitor-counting tool) as the last line of the third-party services section.
A Google "pref" cookie line as the last line of the cookies section. Cookies are small files saved in a visitor's browser.
3. **Generate** the terms and conditions with Shopify's terms generator. Skip the trial (the free trial of Shopify). Enter company and website information. Receive the document by email.
4. **Review** the generated terms, modify anything needed, then **publish** them on the store.
5. **Create** or confirm a contact page with at least **two contact methods**, for example phone number and business email, optionally Shopify's contact form (a form visitors fill in).
6. **Create** a shipping policy stating when orders ship, average transit time (time on the road), shipping cost, and any free or upgraded shipping options.
7. **Create** a refund and return policy stating the refund rules, how to request a refund, how returns work, and how a return is started.

8. **Link** all five pages in the footer menu.
9. **Add** two contact methods to the footer.
10. **Confirm** that accepted payment methods are displayed in the footer.
Publish order (second method)
1. Go to Settings > Policies (the legal settings page).
For each policy (return and refund, privacy, terms of service, shipping, contact information), either **turn on** the automated policy option (Shopify keeps the text up to date for you)
or **click** Insert template (Shopify adds ready text that you must edit).
**Replace** every placeholder (a marked blank such as a bracketed label) with your real business details: trading name (the name you trade under), business address, business phone number

and contact information.
4. **Click Save**, then **Publish** for each policy.
Shopify has free privacy policy and terms generators. They ask for company information.
They send the generated document by email, so you can paste it onto the policy pages.
**Shopify Policy Generator** (shopify.com/tools/policy-generator): enter company name, email address, business address and website link.
Shopify emails a ready-made privacy policy or terms text that can be pasted without changes. Other generators on the same page create refund and terms texts.
**Privacy generator, skip-trial step**: at the bottom of the page, click the link labelled "I'll skip the Shopify trial now, just create my policy".
Enter the company information and click "send me my privacy policy" to receive the generated document by email.
Generated text **changes over time**. Regenerate privacy and terms pages from the current generator. Replace older text when the generator updates.
**Check** the generated privacy policy regularly against the current store setup.
a privacy policy from Shopify's generator, used with only a few modifications, was roughly **95%** standard Shopify text.
Automated policy or template
**Use automated policy (an on/off toggle)**
How to use it: Settings > Policies, open the policy, turn on "Use automated policy", click Save

Behaviour: Text stays in sync with your store settings and Shopify's latest templates and updates on its own. Still check that business details are correct
Ids: ,,

**Insert template**
How to use it: Click Insert template (Terms of Service), or Create from template (privacy, terms)

Behaviour: Static text (fixed text that does not update by itself). You replace every placeholder and edit the text yourself
Ids: ,,,
The automated option exists on each policy page under Settings > Policies.
Creating a page from a template means you confirm that you have read the template disclaimer (a warning that the text is only a starting point).
**Shopify admin steps** (template route). Shopify admin is Shopify's back office.

1. Click Settings in the bottom left corner of the Shopify Admin.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the Settings page and click Policies.

3. In the Privacy policy section, click Create from template.
4. Read the highlighted instructions at the top of the generated text.

5. Delete the highlighted instructions after reading them.
6. Enter **today's date** as the last updated date.

7. Replace the generic example domain with your store's actual URL (web address).
8. Edit any other template parts that refer to your business.

**Automated route**: go to Settings > Policies, click Privacy policy, turn on the **Use automated policy** toggle at the top, then click Save. The same toggle is described as Turn on the automated policy option.
Editing the content
Delete the "notes to merchant" section **for now**. It applies only once you run ads. Update the privacy policy with ad-specific details before ads go live.
In the contact section, delete any phone number or physical location you do not yet have. **Keep an email address** there. The default is the email used at Shopify sign-up.
It can be changed in the same place at any time.
Add the extra privacy text if it is missing: the remarketing sentence, the Google Analytics sentence and the Google "pref" cookie line described in the compliance order.
The privacy policy should cover data privacy and security as part of the full legal section.
The trade name (DBA, "doing business as", the name you sell under) is used as the store name in terms and privacy policies.

The author gives no legal advice on whether the LLC name (the legal company name, such as a US limited liability company) must be included. Older (2023).
Conflicting values, both kept:
Practice: use the DBA as the store name and do **not** add the LLC name. Applies where the author's practice is followed.
Caution: the privacy policy may need to name **both** the store name and the legal LLC name, since they often differ. Unverified.
A lawyer should confirm the exact wording required in your jurisdiction (the country or state where you operate). Older (2021).
The ready-made policy set (terms, shipping, returns, customer support and data protection) contains **no privacy policy text**.
Shopify's written policies list still expects a Privacy policy page, so write and publish it separately.
Terms of service: Creating the page

**Shopify admin steps** (Insert template route):
1. Go to Settings > Policies.

2. Click Insert template. Shopify generates the full policy.
3. Replace any bracketed placeholders with your business name and support email.

4. Optionally leave address and phone number blank.
5. Click Save.
**Full template procedure**:
1. Go to Settings > Policies.

2. In the Terms of service section, click Create from template.
3. Replace the sentence that names the operator of the website with your store name.

4. Read the whole text and replace every generic item with your own information.
5. Remove references to policies you have not created yet, such as the refund policy.
6. Replace the link to the privacy policy with a real link to the Privacy Policy you just created.

7. Fill in the contact information section with your details, or remove lines that do not apply.
8. Click Save.
**Shorter variant**:

1. Go to Settings > Policies and click Terms of service.
2. Click Insert template at the top to have Shopify generate the template.
3. Replace the link to privacy policy placeholder with a link to the Privacy Policy page you created.

4. Replace the trading name placeholder with the store name.
5. Replace the contact email placeholder with the support email address.

6. Leave the business address and phone number fields empty if only an email address is provided.
7. Click Save.
Both variants above describe the same Shopify route. Their wording differs, and both are kept.
Terms set the rules for using the website and buying products. They should cover payment, shipping, returns and warranties (promises to repair or replace).
The terms should state that the store **may update them at any time** and that changes are posted on the page.
They should also cover correct use of the site, prohibited activities (things not allowed) and age restrictions.
Standard template text. Use it as a starting point and edit it to fit your business:
Terms and Conditions By visiting our website and buying products from us, you agree to follow these terms and conditions.
This includes correct use of the site, activities that are not allowed, and age restrictions. We may change these terms at any time, and any changes will be posted on this page.
Publishing and reading
The generated terms are the store's **real legal terms**, not placeholder text.
Read them, adjust anything that does not fit the business, and only then publish.
In one store the generated terms were published unchanged. The owner must still read them before going live.
Templates are a starting point. Edit each one to match how your business handles orders, refunds and customer data before publishing.
**Remove** any reference to a policy you have not built yet. **Link** the privacy policy to the real page.
1. In Shopify Admin, go to Settings and select Policies. Open Shipping Policy.
p.h: Shipping policy: Creating the policy (Shopify route)

p.t: 2. Get the **Shipping Policy AI Prompt** (a ready instruction for an AI writing tool) that starts with "You are a professional e-commerce operations copywriter". Copy it completely.
The full text of this prompt is not included here, so take it verbatim from the prompt file and do **not rewrite it**.
Fill in the **Student Inputs** (the blanks the prompt asks you to fill): store name, support email address (use support@yourdomain.com format), shipping region, handling time (time to pack
and send the order), transit time (time on the road), delivery timeframe, and shipping method details.

4. Use the **standard timeframes** below unless different circumstances apply.
5. Create the policy using the prompt. Insert the generated policy into Shopify and save.

**Handling (packing and sending)**
Standard timeframe: **3-5 business days** (working days)
**Transit (on the road)**

Standard timeframe: **3-7 business days**
**Total delivery**
Standard timeframe: **7-12 business days**
Dropshipping timeframes (the supplier ships straight to the customer)

**Processing time**
Value: **1-3 business days**

**USA delivery**
Value: **7-12 business days**
**UK delivery**
Value: **5-10 business days**

**Australia and New Zealand delivery**
Value: **7-15 business days**
**European countries delivery**
Value: **6-10 business days**
These figures are rough estimates in business days. **Before publishing, replace them** with the delivery times your supplier and carrier (the delivery company) actually achieve.
Promises the store cannot keep lead to customer complaints.
Which figure applies: the standard table applies to the usual case. The dropshipping table applies to supplier-fulfilled stores, as the source describes them.
Both values are given here so you can choose the one that matches your supply chain.
Example values from 2026: orders leave in **2-3 working days** and reach customers in **6-10 days**.
Shipping methods, estimated delivery times, shipping costs and international shipping details, and
p.h: What the shipping policy must contain

p.t: which customs duties (import taxes) or taxes the customer must pay.
Processing time, delivery times per country, shipping fees charged, and the domestic shipping time for the store's home country.
When orders ship, average transit time, shipping cost, and any free or upgraded shipping options.

Confirmation and tracking email, how shipping rates are calculated at checkout, which countries are served and how international shipping times can differ, and that customs or weather can delay delivery.
If the offer includes free shipping, **state it clearly**. Make the shipping cost terms transparent.
Google Shopping (Google's product listings) requires the customer to know the **exact shipping cost before checkout begins**.
A free-shipping header must be matched by an explicit free-shipping statement in the shipping policy. Vague wording about shipping costs is a common reason for Merchant Center flags.
If products are built for one market, **say so on the shipping page**. For example, say that they need a 110V electrical system (the US power standard) and are certified only to US standards.
This protects the store from electrical-compatibility complaints from buyers elsewhere. It is a condition-specific notice, not a general legal disclaimer. Older (2021-22).
What the shipping policy must contain (continued)
Shipping and refund policies must be shown in checkout with the company name and at least an email address.
Text for the shipping policy prompt, with placeholders (marked blanks to fill in), from 2026:
Write a shipping policy for my Shopify store called [Your Store Name]. Orders are shipped within [X-X] working days and usually arrive within [X-X] working days.
Cover the processing time, the confirmation and tracking email, how shipping rates are calculated at checkout, which countries are served and how international shipping times can differ,
and that delivery can be delayed by customs or weather. Use [placeholders] for any values I have not given you.
Second shipping prompt, for a store with known figures, from 2026:
Draft a shipping policy for my Shopify store, [Your Store Name]. Orders leave our hands in 2-3 working days and reach customers in 6-10 days.
The text must cover processing time, how checkout calculates shipping rates, international shipping, and the tracking email sent when an order ships. State that customs or weather can delay delivery.
Put [placeholders] wherever I haven't supplied a figure.
1. In Shopify Admin, go to Settings > Policies.
p.h: Refund, return and exchange policy: Creating the policy (Shopify route)

p.t: 2. Click **Return and Refund Policy**.
3. Use the **Return & Refund Policy AI Prompt** (a ready instruction for an AI writing tool). Its full text is not included here, so take it verbatim from the prompt file.

return window (the number of days a customer has to send an item back; recommended: **30 days**);
condition requirements;

damage reporting timeframe (how long a customer has to report damage).
5. Leave most other defaults as-is for now.
6. **Generate** the policy.

7. **Paste** into Shopify.
8. **Click Save**.
Return window: values by context

**Standard recommendation**
Window: **30 days**, no restocking fee

Applies when: Default for a new store
**Dropshipping, defect cases**
Window: **14 or 30 days** money-back guarantee (you get your money back for faulty items)

Applies when: Defective (faulty), damaged or not-as-described items. Chinese suppliers usually do not accept returns
Ids: ,

**30-day guarantee in sales**
Window: **30-day** money-back guarantee

Applies when: Removes purchase risk (fear of losing money); shown near the purchase decision
**EU shipping**

Window: **14-day** right to cancel or return for any reason
Applies when: Applies whenever the store ships into the EU (European Union), even if the normal window is shorter
Make the **30-day guarantee visible** near the purchase decision.
If the store ships into the EU, **keep the 14-day right** to cancel or return for any reason in the returns policy. Keep it even when the normal return window is shorter.
Chinese suppliers usually do not accept returns. But they do refund or replace items that arrive damaged, defective or not as described.
The return policy should therefore offer a 14-day or 30-day money-back guarantee for these cases only.
Dropshipping clause to adapt. Replace the bracketed placeholder with your support email and choose 14 or 30 days:
We provide a 14-day (or 30-day) money-back guarantee if you receive a defective, damaged product or if the product is not as described.
Please contact us at [support email] and we will do our best to help. Please send us a photo or video as proof so our team can investigate.
If our team approves your request, we will issue a full refund or a replacement, as agreed.
Return address and return conditions
For a new store without a return address, the owner's own address or a **virtual address** (a mail-forwarding address,
not a real office) can be used as the return address (where items are sent back to). **Customers pay** the return shipping label (the prepaid postage sticker).
A returned item is accepted **only if** it is in good condition with intact (not broken), unopened packaging. Add these conditions to the return policy.
If you have no return address, remove or change that line in the generated policy.

Rules for refunds, exchanges and returns, the conditions for returns, time limits and any restocking fees.
The policy should cover:

Refund rules, how to request a refund, how returns work, and how a return is started.
Return prompt, from 2026:
Write a return and refund policy for my Shopify store called [Your Store Name].
Cover eligibility, the return window in days from the date of purchase, the proof of purchase requirement, non-returnable item types, how refunds are processed and how long they take,
when partial refunds apply, when exchanges are allowed, who pays return shipping and whether it is refundable, the rules for sale items, and how customers can contact us.
Use [placeholders] for any values I have not given you, and keep the wording plain and customer-friendly.
Specific product risks
Fashion products have **high return rates**, so return and shipping policies must be clear before launch.
Suppliers should also agree to refund defective or wrong-size items.
**Do not copy** another store's policy. Write the refund, return and shipping text from your actual return window, conditions and exceptions.
Check it against consumer rules (laws that protect buyers) in each country you sell to.

Before writing your own return and shipping policies, review established dropshipping stores' policies as a reference. Adapt the structure to your own supplier terms rather than copying their wording.
The policy should **protect the business** while being **fair to customers**.
Open Shopify Admin > Settings > Policies.

Click the policy you need (for example Return and refund policy) to generate the default template.
Replace the store's contact email with your support email.

Insert a return address if you have one. Otherwise, remove or change that line.
Adjust any other line to your needs.
Copy the finished text into a page, or save it in the policies section.
Shopify, the online store software you use, gives every store a default contact page.
p.h: Contact page and contact details: Contact page

p.t: Add its link to the footer, the strip at the bottom of every page.
The default page named Contact is already there: go to **Online Store > Pages > Add page**. If the store is locked with a password, remove the password before you check the page.
Create or confirm a contact page with at least **two contact methods**, for example a phone number and a business email. You can also add Shopify's contact form.
Use a **business email**, not a personal email, on the contact page and in the footer.
Use a support mailbox on the store's own domain (your web address), for example support@yourstorename.com. Use the same address in the return policy, shipping policy and contact page.
Make sure someone reads it.
Minimum contact details: sources compared
**Google (contact information rule)**

Minimum required: At least two methods, recommended email plus phone, with business hours
Notes: Address not required for this model. Email and phone must be real and working

**Google (general expectation)**
Minimum required: At least two of: physical address, phone number, email address

Notes: Phone plus email meets the requirement without a physical address
**Cross-border minimum**

Minimum required: Email is essential; business address and phone are optional
Notes: Use the email in every policy
**Source B**
Minimum required: Three details: phone number, email address, postal address
Notes: Phone and address should also appear in the footer. Google may check these on the site
Google's contact information rule and its general expectation both accept **a phone plus email**, with no address needed.
The 2021-22 source asks for **all three** details. It is older, so treat it as the stricter option, not as the current rule.
1. Open the policy in **Shopify Settings > Policies**, then scroll to the contact information section.
2. Click the **template** option. A template is a ready-made text, and this one fills in your store details for you.

3. Confirm the email address uses your real domain. It can be a support or sales address.
4. Add a phone number, labelled as a call option.
5. Add your **hours of operation**, for example 9am through 5pm EST (Eastern Standard Time, a US time zone).

6. Check that there is **no placeholder text** (dummy text left in by mistake). Then click **publish**.
A physical address is **not needed** in this section.

For a US-based store, a valid hours entry can read 9am through 5pm EST, with the time zone stated. Only the contact section of the policies needs this. Customers rarely see it, but Google's crawler reads it.
A crawler is Google's robot that reads your pages.
Every email address and phone number in policies and contact pages must be **real and current**.
In every policy page, use your correct real email address and real phone number. Remove any "555" placeholder phone number. Delete all bracketed or template filler text.
Footer, menus and visibility: Footer content
Create and link these pages in the footer menu **before you launch traffic** (visitors arriving from ads or search):
privacy policy (use a Privacy Policy Generator), terms and conditions (use a Terms and Conditions Generator),

contact us, shipping policy, refunds and exchanges.
Add **two contact methods** to the footer.
Show the **accepted payment methods** in the footer.
Link the refund, privacy, terms of service and shipping policy pages in the footer **before you submit to Google**.
The refund, shipping, privacy and terms pages should appear in the footer Quick Links menu, a small link menu, and must not be hidden. Make them easy to find **before you run paid ads**.

These pages are required parts of the storefront (the part of the store customers see).
Put a footer link to the policy pages so customers can find them easily.
The footer phone number and address should match the Contact Us page details.
Create the menu under **Online Store > Navigation > Add menu**. Name it, for example, "Our policies".
Add a menu item for each policy page: Privacy policy, Terms of service, Shipping policy, Return and refund policy, and optionally Contact. Then click **Save menu**.

In the theme footer:
1. Go to **Online Store > Themes > Customize**.
2. Open the footer section in the theme editor.

3. Click **Add block**, choose Menu, and select the policy menu.
4. Rename the heading from "Quick links" to "Our policies".

5. Check that all policy links appear in the footer, then save.
Main menu dropdown. A dropdown is a menu item that opens a list:

1. In the main menu, click **Add menu item** and name it Our Company.
2. Link it to the About Us page.
3. Drag the item under Our Company so it becomes a dropdown.

4. Add the child items Contact Us, Shipping, Easy Returns, Price Match, Privacy and Terms of Service. Link each one to its matching page.
5. Click **Save menu**.
Make the refund and return policy clear and easy to find. The website footer is a recommended place for it.
Terms and privacy pages must be easy for customers to find. Some traffic platforms refuse to run ads without easy access.
Policies saved under Settings are also linked in the checkout footer. Add the pages and footer links afterwards, so visitors can find them.
Checkout legal settings: How the checkout gets its policies
The checkout (the page where customers pay) is hosted separately from your main site.
Footer links do not appear there. So **enter the legal policies separately**, even though the checkout looks like it is on your domain. Older (2021-22).
Policies entered in Shopify's policy settings are the texts linked at checkout. Fill them in there first to meet the checkout requirement.
Policies in the legal settings are linked in the checkout footer. They do **not** appear automatically in the storefront footer, so add them to your online store menus.
Legal pages must be visible in the checkout, because customers enter personal and card details there.
**Publish each policy after you save it.** Each policy shows "No policy set" until you add one.
**Source B**

Menu name in admin: Settings > Legal, which lists refund, privacy, terms of service and shipping policies, each with a Create from template button
Date: 2021-22

Ids: ,
**Source C**
Menu name in admin: Settings > Policies: return, privacy, terms of service, shipping and contact information

Date: 2026

Menu name in admin: Settings > Policies (the legal settings page)

Date: 2026
Use the menu name your admin shows. "Admin" is Shopify's back office, where you manage the store. **The policy text must be the same in both places**.

1. Go to **Online Store > Pages** and open the Refund policy page.
2. Select all the text and copy it.
p.h: Copy the policy text into the checkout

p.t:
3. Go to **Settings > Legal** and paste it into the Refund policy box.
4. Repeat for the Privacy policy, Terms of service and Shipping policy pages.

5. Make sure each policy in Legal **matches the text on your site exactly**.
6. Click **Save**.
Do not keep two different versions of the same policy, one on the site and one in the checkout. Pages and the Legal section must contain identical text.
enter the return and shipping policy, privacy policy and terms of service in Settings > Legal. These feed the checkout page, and their text must match the corresponding site pages exactly.
Placeholders, sample values and accuracy: Placeholders to remove
Do not publish a template with unfilled placeholders, such as "(INSERT TRADING NAME)",
"[INSERT BUSINESS ADDRESS]" or "[INSERT BUSINESS PHONE NUMBER]". Replace them with your **real business details** before you publish.
Templates contain bracketed placeholders. Replace each one with real store information before you publish.
Leaving a placeholder, such as the trading name (the name you sell under) or the privacy policy link in the terms, makes the page incomplete.
Shopify's generated policy texts contain bracketed placeholders and instruction notes. Replace every bracket with your store name, contact email and address. Delete the notes before you publish.
Sample values left in a prompt's input fields, such as a template's example brand name, carry into the generated policy or About Us text.
Replace or delete **every sample value** before you paste the output into Shopify.
Placeholder text, bracketed template fields and fake phone numbers such as 555-555-5555 are flagged by Google as signs of an unprofessional or incomplete store.

Shopify's policy generators insert placeholder text. **Check and edit every generated policy**.
Confirm there is **no placeholder text** before you publish.
Suppliers may click through your policies during review. A policy with placeholder links, missing sections or links to pages that do not exist makes the store look incomplete.
Remove or fix every such item **before you submit the store for approval**.
Templates contain placeholders that must be replaced before submission. Review every generated policy under **Shopify Admin > Settings > Policies**.
After a generator (such as ChatGPT, an AI writing tool) writes a policy, reply in the same chat with your real figures.
Ask for a revised version. Include the exact processing days, delivery days, return window and contact email in each revision, so the sample numbers are replaced.
In every policy page, replace the placeholders for the store name, the privacy policy link and the contact email, one at a time.
Accuracy and reality
Policies must describe what the store **actually does**. They must not just exist as placeholders.
In most US states, the core legal pages (privacy policy, terms of service, return and refund policy) are binding legal documents.
Every page has to describe what the shop really does in practice.
Promises the store cannot keep lead to customer complaints. Replace rough delivery estimates with **actual figures** before you publish.
Conditional statements, such as financing availability, exclusions, sales tax by state, or a shipping restriction to certain states, must link to a page that explains the details.
Without that, the visitor becomes confused and worried. Older (2021-22).
Statements such as "Some exclusions apply" or "No shipping to" a state, with no explanation or link, make a store look unreliable.
**State the restriction plainly and explain it**, even when there is a good reason for it. Older (2021-22).
The price match guarantee can be stated clearly as applying to the listed price before coupon codes. This helps customers understand it before they order. Older (2023).
Contact information that Google's crawlers read should list **at least two contact methods**, recommended as email plus phone,
along with business hours. An address is not required for this business model. But the email and phone must be real and working.
Adding a short summary, such as a table or a few key points, to policy pages helps Google's crawlers read the key details, such as return and shipping terms.
Google Merchant Center (Google's account for listing your products) flags accounts automatically when required pages are missing. You must request a **manual review**.
Policy pages must match the policies entered in Google Merchant Center.
Google Ads (Google's paid advertising) requires privacy policy and terms of service pages that match its requirements. **Check them every time the generator updates**.
A missing privacy policy can get your Google Merchant Center account suspended (shut off). Repeated violations can lead to a **permanent ban**.
AI review of policy pages: Review prompt
Paste the policy text directly into the chat. The tool may crawl the live site, which may still show old policies.
Results based on the live site can point to errors that are already fixed.
Hello. I own [your domain] and I am about to submit my website to Google Merchant Center and Google Ads for approval.
Please review the policy pages I paste below, not the live version of the website, and tell me whether anything is not compliant with Google Ads and Google Merchant Center policies.
If you find anything non-compliant or questionable, reply with the exact text in question, why it is a problem and your recommended update. [paste the text of the policy page here]
Thank you for your feedback. I have revised our [policy name] and pasted the new version below.
Please check this revised text against Google Merchant Center and Google Ads policies and tell me whether it is compliant.
If anything is still questionable, reply with the exact sentence, the reason it is a problem and your recommended wording. [paste the revised policy text here]
1. Send **one policy page** to Google Gemini (Google's AI chat tool) and ask for a compliance review.
p.h: Review procedure, one page at a time

p.t:
2. Read every issue it lists, including the exact sentence and the recommended update.
3. **Apply every recommended change** to that policy in Shopify.
4. Paste the revised policy back to Gemini and ask for a second check.
5. Repeat until Gemini reports the policy as fully compliant. Then move to the next policy page.
Repeat this process for the refund policy, shipping policy, privacy policy and terms of service.
Country-specific content
For the four main markets (US, Canada, Australia and the UK), add the required privacy policy and terms text to the legal pages.
Other countries, especially in Europe, have separate rules that must be added too.

If the store ships into the European Union, keep the **14-day right to cancel or return for any reason** in the returns policy. This is a cooling-off right, meaning the customer can change their mind.
Check the consumer rules in **each country you sell to** when you write refund, return and shipping text.
Customs duties and taxes that the customer must pay belong in the shipping policy. Customs duties are import fees charged at the border.
In the US, the core legal pages are binding in most states. State-specific wording, such as for California, must be checked with a legal source. Do not assume it. Older (2022).
A product built for one market needs a clear notice on the shipping page. For example, a product for 110V electrical systems (US-style voltage) needs a US-only certification note. Older (2021-22).
Legal pages are **not legal advice**.
Have a lawyer review the privacy policy, terms of service and refund policy, especially for stores with custom situations.
Shopify's legal page templates are not legal advice. You must customise them for your store.
Shopify policy templates are not legal advice. You are responsible for their accuracy and for following the laws that apply to your business.
Create the privacy policy and terms of service in Shopify admin under **Settings > Policies**, not as ordinary pages. This makes Shopify treat them as legal pages.
The links in Google Merchant Center should point to those pages. Older (2023).
Legal ownership details: use the trade name in the policy text, and check the LLC question (an LLC is a US company type) with a lawyer.
Payment and billing terms
The terms, or a separate payment page, should describe how payments are processed, which payment methods are accepted,
and any recurring billing (automatic repeat charges) if you offer subscriptions (plans customers pay for every month).

Payment and billing belong in the terms of service, which should cover payment.
Show the **accepted payment methods** in the footer.
Customers enter personal and card details at checkout, so the legal pages must be visible there.
Legal pages help resolve disputes with customers and payment providers.

Google's rules for ads are the Google ads compliance rules.
Link the policy pages in the **store footer**.

Some countries require a legal notice page with your business details. The Impressum is that page.
The rules below apply in Germany.
In Germany, an online store must show a **legally required legal notice** (Impressum) with the business information on the website.
Missing information can lead to **warning letters** (formal legal warnings) from lawyers and complaints from customers.
The **Impressum** must be complete before the store goes live (open to customers).
Check the **legal requirements** (legal rules) of the country you sell from and the countries you sell to.
**TermsFeed** is an all-in-one wizard tool (a guided, step-by-step tool) recommended by Google for generating privacy policy
agreements without legal expertise (no lawyer knowledge needed).
Google Adwords (Google's advertising platform, now called Google Ads) provides **sample privacy policy templates** (example documents) to use as a starting point.
A store should have a privacy policy and terms of service **live on the site before launch**. These pages are part of the basic legal setup, separate from marketing copy (sales text).
